around.headline: Bengaluru father allegedly kills his two young daughters at a hotel, attempts suicide
around.summary: Police say a man booked a 5-star hotel room, killed his two daughters and attempted suicide, reportedly leaving a note citing marital distress; he is in custody/under treatment. If you or someone you know is in emotional crisis, Tele-MANAS (14416) offers free, confidential counselling round the clock.
around.source: NDTV, The Times of India, The Indian Express

around.headline: Techie missing since Monday on a solo Shivagange trek; drones deployed
around.summary: A Bengaluru techie, weeks away from his wedding, has been missing since setting off alone up Shivagange on Monday, and a search drone has since spotted what may be a body on the hill. Before any solo trek, share your route and expected return time with someone, and check in when you're back.
around.source: The Indian Express, The Times of India, NDTV

around.headline: Bank uncovers ₹4.5 crore loan fraud built on forged documents
around.summary: A Bengaluru bank detected a racket that used forged papers to fraudulently secure loan sanctions worth ₹4.5 crore in other people's names. Pull your free credit report from CIBIL or Experian periodically so you catch any loan opened in your name before it wrecks your score.

around.headline: FDA raids expose hygiene violations at Indira Canteens, KFC, McDonald's and a Zepto warehouse
around.summary: Food safety inspectors found unhygienic conditions at the Bommanahalli and Lingarajpuram Indira Canteens and several big-chain kitchens, and called a Zepto dark-store warehouse 'extremely unhygienic'. Worth checking FSSAI hygiene ratings before ordering from these outlets over the next few days.
around.source: The Times of India, Deccan Herald, NDTV

around.headline: Karnataka government signals a clampdown on bike taxis
around.summary: State authorities are moving to restrict bike-taxi services such as Rapido and Uber Moto, citing safety and regulatory concerns. If bike taxis are part of your daily commute, keep an autorickshaw or metro route in mind as a backup in case services are suspended.

around.headline: Actor Prakash Raj's name reportedly deleted from Bengaluru's electoral rolls under SIR
around.summary: Prakash Raj says his name vanished from the voter list during the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR), and he isn't the only one hitting errors in the draft rolls. Check your own name on the Karnataka CEO website and file a correction now, before the objection window closes.
around.source: The Hindu, The Times of India, NDTV

around.headline: Markets slide as India faces a 100% US tariff threat under Trump
around.summary: The Sensex fell 388 points amid trade tensions, even as a US official said Washington and Delhi are working to resolve a threatened 100% tariff on Indian goods. A prolonged standoff could push up prices of imported goods and pressure trade-linked businesses and jobs.

street_smart.title: You get an SMS saying an EMI payment on a personal loan has bounced — but you never took out that loan. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: Real incident today: a Bengaluru bank detected a ₹4.5 crore loan fraud where a racket used forged documents to fraudulently secure loan sanctions in other people's names (The Times of India).
street_smart.situation: Your phone buzzes with an SMS: an EMI on a personal loan has failed, and you need to pay up immediately or face 'legal action'. Trouble is, you've never applied for any loan. It lands the same week a Bengaluru bank uncovered a racket that used forged KYC papers to sanction loans in strangers' names. What do you do?

choices.text: Call the number in the SMS right away and read out your Aadhaar and PAN details so they can 'verify' it isn't you.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. Numbers in an unsolicited SMS aren't verified — reading out your Aadhaar, PAN, or an OTP to whoever answers hands a fraudster exactly what they need to open, or keep abusing, a loan in your name. Genuine banks never ask you to 'confirm' identity by reading out ID numbers on an inbound call you didn't initiate.

choices.text: Ignore it — you know you never took a loan, so it must just be spam.
choices.feedback: Risky. If someone really did use stolen documents to take a loan in your name, ignoring the message lets missed 'your' EMIs pile up and damage your credit score before you even realise it's happening. A fraudulent loan doesn't disappear just because you never applied for it.

choices.text: Pay the EMI amount mentioned in the SMS immediately to avoid 'legal trouble'.
choices.feedback: Also a trap. Paying doesn't fix identity theft — it just hands money straight to whoever sent the message and gives them a reason to keep billing you. Real banks collect through your actual loan account, never through a link or number texted to you out of the blue.

choices.text: Pull your free credit report from CIBIL or Experian, and if a bogus loan shows up, file a written dispute with the lender's nodal officer and a complaint at cybercrime.gov.in or 1930.
choices.feedback: Correct. Your credit report shows any loan actually opened in your name, regardless of what a random SMS claims. A written dispute with the bank's nodal officer gets the account frozen while it's investigated, and a cybercrime complaint creates a paper trail that helps if the fraud needs to be traced back.

takeaways: Check your free credit report on CIBIL or Experian periodically — it's the only reliable way to catch a loan taken out in your name before it wrecks your score.
Never share Aadhaar, PAN, or OTP with anyone who contacted you first, whether by SMS, call, or WhatsApp — real banks don't verify identity that way.
If a fraudulent loan does show up, complain in writing to the bank's nodal officer and file a report at cybercrime.gov.in or call 1930 — don't just pay to make it go away.

quiz.question: What did a recent CAG report flag about Bengaluru Metro's Phase 1 and 2?
quiz.why: The report flagged land acquisition costs rising by roughly ₹6,603 crore alongside the ridership shortfall — both raise questions about how future metro phases are planned and funded.

quiz.question: Actor Prakash Raj said his name went missing from Bengaluru's voter list during which exercise?
options: The Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls
quiz.why: SIR is a periodic clean-up of the electoral rolls meant to remove duplicate or deceased entries; anyone can check their own name and file a correction on the Karnataka Chief Electoral Officer's website.

quiz.question: The Cauvery Water Management Authority recently directed Karnataka to release how much water daily to Tamil Nadu?
quiz.why: A 'cusec' (cubic feet per second) is the standard unit used to measure river flow in India's long-running inter-state water-sharing disputes.

quiz.question: What does the Sensex actually track?
options: 30 large companies listed on the BSE
quiz.why: The Sensex's counterpart on the National Stock Exchange is the Nifty 50, which tracks 50 large companies instead of 30.

quiz.question: Karnataka's coastline lies along which sea?
quiz.why: Karnataka's roughly 320 km coastline includes New Mangalore Port, one of India's major cargo ports.
